questions.question: Before checking answer options in an analogy question, what should you do first according to the guide's method?
options: State the relationship of the given pair as an explicit rule or sentence
Pick the option that feels most related
Eliminate the shortest option
Assume it is always a synonym relationship
questions.rationale: The guide's core method is to name the relationship explicitly (e.g., 'the structure the first item lives in') before testing options, since a vague sense of relatedness leads to picking loosely-associated but incorrect answers.

questions.question: In the vector-view model of analogy (A, B represented as feature vectors), how is the relationship between A and B represented?
options: As their sum
As their product
As a transformation vector R = B - A, applied to the second pair
Vectors are not used to represent analogy relationships
questions.rationale: The guide's vector view represents the relationship as R = B - A, then applies the same transformation to the second pair (D = C + R), which is especially useful for numerical analogies.

questions.question: If a number analogy pair is 6 : 42, and the rule is 'second = first x (first + 1)', what completes 9 : ?
questions.rationale: Applying the same rule: 9 x (9 + 1) = 9 x 10 = 90.

questions.question: Why might more than one answer option seem to 'sort of' fit an analogy at first glance?
options: Analogy questions always have multiple correct answers
Only classification questions can have this issue
It means the question is flawed
The relationship identified may still be too vague or general — a more specific relationship usually narrows it to one option
questions.rationale: When several options seem to fit, it usually means the stated relationship is too general (e.g., 'both animals' instead of 'predator and its typical prey') — refining it to a more specific rule narrows the answer to exactly one option.

questions.question: What does the 'Analogy Master Table' consolidate?
options: A comprehensive reference of all major relationship categories covered throughout the lesson, for quick lookup
Only number-based relationships
A single isolated example
Only letter-based relationships
questions.rationale: The Analogy Master Table consolidates every major relationship category covered across the lesson into one comprehensive, quick-reference resource.

questions.question: What does the 'Universal Analogy Template' attempt to provide?
options: A single formula only for numbers
A template only for word analogies
A general, reusable framework (state the relationship, test it, verify it) applicable to any analogy type
A rule with no general applicability
questions.rationale: This template provides a general, reusable framework — state the relationship, test it against options, verify it — that applies across any specific analogy type.

questions.question: What does 'Advanced Verification' emphasize, beyond basic verification?
options: Skipping verification when time is short
Rigorously checking the identified relationship against the golden rule and ruling out all known traps before finalizing an answer
Only checking the first option
Verification with no defined process
questions.rationale: Advanced verification goes beyond a basic check, rigorously confirming the relationship against the golden rule while also actively ruling out the specific traps covered earlier in the lesson.

questions.question: What does the 'Master Formula' at this stage of the lesson likely represent?
options: A single narrow formula for one relationship type only
A formula that replaces the need to identify any relationship
A formula unrelated to analogy solving
A distilled, general statement of the core analogy-solving principle, unifying the many specific techniques covered
questions.rationale: The Master Formula distills the core analogy-solving principle into one general, unifying statement, consolidating the many specific techniques covered throughout the lesson.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'Final Exam Cheat Sheet'?
options: To condense every essential rule, trap, and technique from the lesson into one compact, quick-reference summary
To introduce brand-new relationship types
To replace the practice sets
To only summarize the first two parts
questions.rationale: The Final Exam Cheat Sheet condenses every essential concept from across the entire lesson into one compact, easily-reviewable summary.

questions.question: Why does the lesson include four tiers of 'Practice Set — Level 1' through 'Level 4'?
options: To make the lesson unnecessarily long
Because each level uses entirely unrelated skills
To let learners build analogy-solving skill progressively, from simple to increasingly challenging cases
Because only Level 4 is actually relevant to exams
questions.rationale: Progressive practice levels let learners build skill systematically, moving from simple cases toward increasingly challenging ones as understanding solidifies.

questions.question: What is the value of 'High-Level Practice — No Immediate Answers,' compared to the earlier tiered practice sets?
options: It has no additional value
It trains the learner to work through problems without immediately checking the answer, building independent problem-solving confidence
It only repeats the Level 1 practice set
It removes the need for any verification
questions.rationale: Withholding immediate answers trains learners to work through problems independently and build confidence in their own verification process, rather than relying on immediate confirmation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Answer Verification for High-Level Practice' appearing separately, after the practice itself?
options: To replace the need to attempt the practice set
It serves no distinct purpose from the earlier practice answers
To provide the answers before the practice set
To let learners check their independently-derived answers only after genuinely attempting the problems themselves
questions.rationale: Separating verification from the practice set itself ensures learners genuinely attempt the problems independently first, checking their work only afterward.

questions.question: What is an 'Analogy Mind Map' intended to show?
options: An unrelated diagram
How all the individual relationship categories and techniques covered throughout the lesson connect to and build on each other
Only the answers to the practice sets
A single isolated relationship type
questions.rationale: The mind map visually shows how all the individual relationship categories and techniques covered throughout the lesson relate to and build on one another.

questions.question: What is the overarching lesson of this entire 12-part chapter on analogy reasoning?
options: That analogy reasoning is purely a matter of guesswork

That reliably solving analogy problems comes from explicitly identifying the relationship, testing it rigorously against options, and watching for known traps — not from surface-level pattern matching alone
That only number-based analogies matter
That verification can safely be skipped once an answer seems plausible
questions.rationale: The chapter's consistent central lesson is that reliable analogy solving comes from explicitly identifying and rigorously verifying the relationship, actively watching for known traps — not from superficial, surface-level pattern matching.
